subject: DI02000161

body.en:
Understand the idea

Combinational output depends on present inputs;sequential output also depends on stored state.

Explanation and application

  • A combinational adder has no intended memory.A flip-flop stores one bit;its next state is Qnext=f(inputs,Q).Power-up state is not guaranteed unless the device specifies it.
  • A latch is level-sensitive;an edge-triggered flip-flop samples near an active clock transition.They share state tables but differ in when updates are permitted.
  • Setup time is required before the active edge;hold time after it.Propagation delay occurs before outputs settle.Violating timing can cause metastability,not a predictable third logic digit.
  • Asynchronous preset/clear override the clock according to device priority.When inactive,the normal clocked state table applies;simultaneous assertion may be forbidden.
Latch versus flip-flop?

Alevel-sensitive latch follows during enable;an edge-triggered flip-flop samples near the active transition.
body.gu:
વિચાર સમજીએ

Combinational output present inputsપર dependકરે;sequential outputમાં stored stateપણ અસરકરે છે.

સમજણ અને ઉપયોગ

  • Combinational adderમાં intended memoryનથી.Flip-flop એક bit storeકરે;Qnext=f(inputs,Q)છે.Device specify ન કરે ત્યાં power-up state guaranteedનથી.
  • Latch level-sensitive છે;edge-triggered flip-flop active clock transitionનજીક sampleકરે.State tables સમાન હોઈ શકે,પણ update timing જુદું છે.
  • Active edgeપહેલાં setup time તથા પછી hold timeજોઈએ.Output settleથતાં propagation delayથાય.Timing violationથી metastability થઈ શકે;predictable ત્રીજો logic digit નહિ.
  • Asynchronous preset/clear device priority પ્રમાણે clockને overrideકરે.Inactiveહોય ત્યારે normal clocked tableલાગે;બંને એકસાથે assert કરવું forbiddenહોઈ શકે.

Understand the idea

Two cross-coupled NOR gates create feedback that retains a bit after the command is removed.

Explanation and application

  • Connect Q=NOR(R,Qnot)and Qnot=NOR(S,Q).Each output drives the opposite gate input;feedback is the memory mechanism.
  • S=1,R=0forces Q=1(set);S=0,R=1forces Q=0(reset).After returning to00the feedback holds the selected state.
  • S=R=1forces both NOR outputs0,so they are no longer complements.Releasing both together has an indeterminate final state;never use that state as normal operation.
  • A NAND SR latch instead uses active-low commands:11holds and00is forbidden.Do not copy the NOR truth table to a NAND latch.

h.gu: Clocked SR તથા SR Flip-flop Interpretation

body.en:
Understand the idea

The syllabus calls this SR flip-flop;always identify whether the actual circuit is a latch,gated latch or edge-triggered device.

Explanation and application

  • For a clock-enable SR latch,AND S,R with enable before the active-high NOR latch.Enable0forces internal00and holds the state;enable1makes it responsive to S,Rlevels.
  • For an ideal edge-triggered SR model,the same command table is evaluated only at the active edge,not throughout HIGH.Characteristic equation is Qnext=S+R′Q for valid S,R.
  • No active edge means hold,except asynchronous controls.A switch contact bounce can create several edges;use a debounced trainer clock.

વિચાર સમજીએ

Syllabusમાં SRflip-flopશબ્દ છે;actual circuit latch,gated latchકે edge-triggered છે તે સ્પષ્ટ ઓળખો.

સમજણ અને ઉપયોગ

  • Clock-enable SRlatchમાં S,Rને enableસાથે ANDકરી NORlatchમાં આપો.Enable0માં internal00અને hold;enable1માં S,Rlevelsપ્રતિ responsiveછે.
  • Ideal edge-triggered SRmodelમાં command table active edgeપર જ evaluateથાય,આખા HIGH દરમિયાન નહિ.Valid S,Rમાટે Qnext=S+R′Qછે.
  • Active edge ન હોય તો hold,સિવાય asynchronous controls.Switch contact bounceથી અનેક edgesથઈ શકે;debounced trainer clockલો.

Feedback is a real connection between two gate outputs and opposite gate inputs,not merely a descriptive block label.

Explanation and application

  • Apply a valid set/reset command to establish a known state before testing hold;power-up alone is not a defined reset procedure.

Understand the idea

Two cascaded storage sections respond on opposite clock phases;the output does not feed through both at once.

Explanation and application

  • In the illustrated teaching model,the master is enabled at CLK=1and the slave at CLK=0;an inverter creates the opposite phase.Nonoverlap is needed in a real implementation.
  • During HIGH,the master resolves the J,Krequest using the stable slave output while the slave holds Q.On HIGH→LOW,the master closes and the slave transfers its stored result.
  • With J=K=1and valid stable inputs,the output toggles once per complete clock cycle rather than racing repeatedly during HIGH.
  • This falling-transfer teaching model is not a promise about every7476variant.Check actual clock/preset/clear timing and input-stability requirements;some master stages can catch input pulses during their open phase.
  • Applications:single-bit registers,event storage,divide-by-two and counters.Flip-flops alone do not debounce a mechanical switch or make asynchronous signals safe without a designed interface.

Aim

Instruments and preparation

  • Use the approved low-voltage current-limited trainer,verified logic ICs/breadboard,defined input switches,logic probe or high-impedance meter,and exact device datasheet.A simulated/numerical practical needs its stated tools instead.
  • Check package orientation and recommended VCCbefore connecting.Power OFFfor wiring;do not apply a9Vbattery directly to74LSlogic;trainer0–30Vcapability is not an IC operating rating.

Circuit connections / setup

Build the active-high cross-coupled NORlatch;record explicitly if the assigned hardware instead uses a clocked or active-low NANDSRvariant.

Procedure

  1. Derive the expected table first;declare bit order,active polarity and any enable/clock assumptions.
  2. Inspect the unpowered connections against the labelled logic diagram and approved pin map;verify common ground and a suitable local decoupling capacitor.
  3. Test set,hold,reset,hold in that order.Avoid simultaneous forbidden commands;explain their predicted behaviour analytically.
  4. Read each output after settling;for sequential circuits record current state,command,clock event and next state separately.
  5. On a mismatch,stop and trace supply,input definition,polarity and intermediate nodes;power OFFbefore changing wiring.
  6. Save genuine results and explain each discrepancy;power down safely.Do not fill actual observations with expected numbers or claim an unperformed experiment.

Expected calculations and interpretation

SRactive-high:00hold,01reset,10set,11forbidden.

Fault finding

Unexpected repeated toggles suggest clock bounce or wrong triggering assumptions;stuck outputs suggest asserted preset/clear or missing supply.Verify before rewiring.

Precautions

  • Never short outputs or exceed ratings;unused inputs must be defined.Output LEDloads need a checked driver/current limiter;an LEDwired to VCCmay indicate logicLOWwhen lit.
  • Use only isolated approved low-voltage apparatus;do not connect mains to logic circuits.A safe trainer is not a guarantee against reversed supply or incorrect pinout.
